categories.title: Goalkeeping
categories.intro: With one dedicated keeper in the squad, pair these with an outfield player in gloves so the keeper always has a partner and a second player learns the basics.

drills.title: Free-movement jog
drills.setup: Mark a 25 by 20 metre box with four cones. All thirteen players jog freely inside it while you call out movements every twenty seconds: heel flicks, side steps, open the hip, backwards jog, half-pace sprint to a corner. Players must avoid contact and keep their heads up, so the box teaches scanning before any ball appears.
drills.coachingPoints: Gradual build from jog to 70 per cent pace; ankles, knees and hips all moving; eyes up, never two players in the same gap.
drills.progression: Shrink the box by five metres so players work harder to find space.

drills.title: Circle passing warm-up
drills.setup: Five players stand evenly spaced on a circle about eight metres across, with a sixth alongside whoever starts with the ball. The ball goes clockwise to the next player, and the passer jogs straight across to join them. That player then passes on and follows in the same way, so two players are always at the ball and no spot is left empty.
drills.coachingPoints: Firm pass along the ground; open the body towards the next player before the ball arrives; jog straight to the spot rather than round the circle; call the receiver's name.
drills.progression: Two touches maximum, then one touch; once that is comfortable, reverse the direction of the circle.

drills.title: Mirror pairs
drills.setup: Pair players up facing each other two metres apart along a cone line. One leads with side steps, drop steps and short shuffles; the partner mirrors the movement without crossing the line. Swap the leader every thirty seconds. Six pairs plus the goalkeeper working with you covers the squad.
drills.coachingPoints: Low stance, weight on the balls of the feet, short quick steps rather than long strides.
drills.progression: Leader carries a ball, so the mirror becomes early defensive footwork.

drills.title: Shark attack
drills.setup: Mark three zones with cones: a safe zone at each end and a larger zone in the middle. All the outfield players but two start in one safe zone with a ball each, and the two sharks start in the middle with no ball. On your call the dribblers cross to the far safe zone while the sharks try to kick balls out of the area. Anyone who loses their ball becomes a shark for the next round. Run five rounds.
drills.coachingPoints: Look for the gap before setting off; change speed rather than run in a straight line; protect the ball with the far foot.
drills.progression: Sharks must win the ball and dribble it out rather than kick it away.

drills.title: Traffic lights
drills.setup: Mark a box with four cones, every player with a ball. Green means dribble at pace, amber means slow and small touches, red means stop the ball dead with the sole of the foot. Call the colours in an unpredictable order and gradually shorten the gaps between calls so the group has to listen while moving.
drills.coachingPoints: Ball always within a stride; stop it dead, do not stand on it; heads up so nobody collides on a red.
drills.progression: Add a fourth call, blue, meaning turn and go the other way.

drills.title: Pass and stretch
drills.setup: Pairs stand eight metres apart with one ball. They pass firmly along the ground for thirty seconds, then on your call the ball is trapped underfoot and both players hold a stretch you name for fifteen seconds: calf, hamstring, quad, hip flexor. Passing resumes as soon as the stretch ends, and you cycle through all four.
drills.coachingPoints: Ball dead before anybody stretches; hold the stretch still, no bouncing; breathe out into it and keep the passing accurate when it restarts.
drills.progression: Increase the distance to fifteen metres so the pass needs more from the standing leg.

drills.title: Cone slalom gates
drills.setup: Set a line of five cones with an even gap between each one and queue the group behind the first cone. Players dribble through the slalom using the inside and outside of the same foot, turn at the end cone and return down the outside of the lane to rejoin the queue. Emphasise close touches through the cones and one longer push out of the last gate. Run two or three lanes side by side if you have the cones for it.
drills.coachingPoints: Small touches, knees bent, ball inside the frame of the body; head up between gates.
drills.progression: Race two lanes against each other, one point per clean run with no cone touched.

drills.title: Four-corner turns
drills.setup: One 20 by 15 metre box with a numbered cone in each corner and a ball for every player. Players dribble in the middle of the box; when you call a number they take the ball to that corner, perform a named turn at the cone and come back out. Cycle through inside hook, outside hook, drag back and Cruyff turn so every player practises all four.
drills.coachingPoints: Slow into the turn, explode out of it; drop the shoulder before turning; two touches maximum to change direction.
drills.progression: Call two corners at once so players plan a route through traffic.

drills.title: Traffic jam
drills.setup: Mark a tight box with four cones and squeeze all twelve outfield players inside it, each with a ball. They dribble continuously in a deliberately crowded space, reacting to your calls of stop, change direction, swap balls or sole of the foot. The tight area forces short touches and constant scanning, and no player can dribble in a straight line for long.
drills.coachingPoints: Head up, no collisions; use both feet; stop the ball dead on the call.
drills.progression: Remove two balls so four players hunt possession while the rest keep theirs.

drills.title: Dribble duels to gates
drills.setup: Mark one pitch and use four cones to make two gates on the defender's end line. The attacker starts at the far end with the ball and has fifteen seconds to dribble through either gate; the defender starts a few metres in front and tries to win it. Swap roles every go and rotate opponents after three attempts each.
drills.coachingPoints: Attack the defender's front foot; commit them with a feint before changing direction; accelerate the moment the gap opens.
drills.progression: Two points for the far gate, so the attacker must move the defender first.

drills.title: Gate dribbling
drills.setup: Scatter a handful of small gates made from cone pairs across the area, all facing different directions. Players dribble freely and score a point for every gate they pass through cleanly, but they cannot use the same gate twice in a row. Ninety seconds per round, three rounds, players count their own score.
drills.coachingPoints: Choose the next gate while still travelling; change direction with the outside of the foot; keep the ball close in the crowd.
drills.progression: Two players share a ball and must both pass through the gate.

drills.title: Shielding the ball
drills.setup: Pairs work inside a small circle marked with four cones, one ball between them. The player in possession has to keep the ball inside the circle for twenty seconds while the partner applies real but fair pressure. Swap on the whistle. The tight space means the only way to survive is to put the body between opponent and ball.
drills.coachingPoints: Arm across, side on, ball on the far foot; feel where the opponent is rather than looking; roll away from pressure, do not turn into it.
drills.progression: Shrink the circle, or add a target cone the holder must reach.

drills.title: Two-touch squares
drills.setup: Mark a square with four cones and put five players on it, one on each corner and a spare queued behind the starting corner, with one ball. Players pass around the square in one direction with a maximum of two touches, then follow their pass and join the back of the corner they played into. The spare means the corner a passer leaves is refilled by the player queued behind, so every corner always has someone to receive. Change direction on your whistle.
drills.coachingPoints: First touch across the body into space; pass with the inside of the foot and follow through low; weight the pass so it arrives at a controllable pace.
drills.progression: One touch only, or add a second ball travelling the other way.

drills.title: Rondo four against two
drills.setup: Mark two grids with a cone on each corner. Four players work on the sides of the grid and cannot come inside; two defenders work in the middle. The outside four keep the ball, moving along their own side to open a passing angle and aiming for ten consecutive passes. Whoever loses the ball swaps with the defender who won it. Run two grids of six and give the goalkeeper a set on the outside.
drills.coachingPoints: Move along your side to create a passing angle; look for the split pass through the middle; one or two touches only.
drills.progression: Add a free player inside the grid who must be found once every five passes.

drills.title: Y-shape pass and move
equipment: 4 cones and 1 ball per Y shape
drills.setup: Lay out a Y with a starting cone, a middle cone twelve metres ahead and two cones splitting left and right another twelve metres on. The first player passes into the middle player, who sets it back or turns and plays wide, then sprints to fill the next cone. Every player follows their pass one station forward, so the pattern rotates itself. Two Y shapes keep the whole squad moving.
drills.coachingPoints: Check away then come to receive; call for it before the pass leaves; play the way you are facing unless you have already turned.
drills.progression: The wide player finishes with a first-time cross into a small goal.

drills.title: Switch the channels
drills.setup: Split a 40 by 30 metre area into three horizontal channels with cones. Play six against six with the rule that the ball must be passed into all three channels before a goal counts. Players may move freely between channels. This turns short passing into a habit of looking for the far side rather than always playing forward.
drills.coachingPoints: Scan before receiving; a long switch needs a firm, driven pass; the receiving player should already be in the empty channel.
drills.progression: Limit the team in possession to three touches each.

drills.title: Third-man runs
drills.setup: Four players per group working towards a goal: a starter, a middle player set square and short, and a third man high on the far side, with the fourth waiting behind the start. The first player passes into the middle player, who sets it back; the first player then plays long to the third man, who has started their run as the set-back leaves and finishes on goal. Everyone rotates one place forward each repetition. Two groups run side by side.
drills.coachingPoints: The runner starts as the set-back is played, not when the pass arrives; the middle player sets it into the passer's stride; call early.
drills.progression: Add a defender who tries to intercept the long pass.

drills.title: One-touch end zones
drills.setup: A pitch with a marked end zone at each end. Play five against five; a point is scored when a player receives a pass inside the opposition end zone. Defenders cannot enter their own end zone, so the game becomes a repeated exercise in timing a pass into space rather than at feet.
drills.coachingPoints: Pass into the space ahead of the runner; wait for the run before releasing; the receiver must not enter the zone early.
drills.progression: Two touches maximum, or the receiving pass must travel along the ground.

drills.title: Two-touch finish
drills.setup: Four cones mark a receiving zone out to one side, with a gate of two cones in front of the keeper. A server at the top and a server at the bottom take turns feeding a ball into the zone. One player receives it in the zone, carries it to the gate, and must shoot with their second touch after going through it. Rotate receiver, server, server so everybody takes each job.
drills.coachingPoints: First touch out of the feet and forward; head still and laces through the middle of the ball; pick a corner before you shoot.
drills.progression: One touch only, or shoot within three seconds of the serve.

drills.title: Cross and finish
drills.setup: Two wide starting cones level with the edge of the penalty area, and two attackers waiting centrally, one at the near post and one at the back post. The wide player dribbles to the corner cone and crosses; the two attackers time their runs to attack near and far. Rotate wide player, near post, back post, then join the queue. Alternate the side each repetition.
drills.coachingPoints: Cross in front of the goal, not at the keeper; attackers start their run late and arrive at speed; near post attacks anything low and early.
drills.progression: Add one recovering defender so attackers must find space, not just the ball.

drills.title: Turn and shoot
drills.setup: The attacker stands sixteen metres from goal with their back to it. A server twelve metres behind them plays a firm pass into their feet. The attacker takes one touch to turn out of the pass, either side, and shoots within two more touches. Add a passive defender at half pressure once players are comfortable turning.
drills.coachingPoints: Check over your shoulder before the ball arrives; touch across the body away from pressure; get the shot away early rather than perfectly.
drills.progression: The defender goes fully live, making it a one against one from a turn.

drills.title: Rapid-fire ladder
drills.setup: Three queues at fourteen metres, one central and one on each angle, with a ball at every cone. On your call the queues shoot in sequence, left, centre, right, one shot every three seconds. The keeper faces continuous work and shooters learn to hit the target quickly. Score one point per goal and keep a team total across two rounds.
drills.coachingPoints: Low and hard beats high and hopeful; strike across the ball from the angles; follow the shot in for a rebound.
drills.progression: Call the queues in a random order so shooters must stay switched on.

drills.title: One against one to goal
drills.setup: The attacker starts twenty metres out with the ball, one defender in front, and both work inside a fifteen-metre-wide channel with the keeper in goal. The attacker has eight seconds to score. Roles swap after each attempt and the pair goes to the back of the queue, so nobody stands still for long.
drills.coachingPoints: Attack at speed but under control; shoot early if the defender opens their stance; follow in for the rebound.
drills.progression: Winner stays on and defends against the next attacker.

drills.title: Combination finish
drills.setup: Two attackers start twenty-five metres out with one defender and the keeper. They must combine, either a wall pass or an overlap, before anybody shoots, and a goal only counts if two players touched the ball in the move. Four attempts per pair, then rotate so everyone plays both roles.
drills.coachingPoints: Pass and move immediately; the supporting run goes past the ball, not behind it; take the shot with the first clear sight of goal.
drills.progression: Add a second defender so the pair must beat a real overload.

drills.title: Press the cone
drills.setup: A cone stands in for the ball ten metres away. Players sprint at it, then slow down over the last three metres and settle into a low sideways-on stance beside it, before shuffling backwards to the start. No ball, no opponent, just the approach and the body shape. Run four repetitions each in two lines.
drills.coachingPoints: Fast approach, slow arrival; last steps short and choppy; sideways on with the front foot pointing the attacker one way.
drills.progression: Replace the cone with a static teammate holding a ball still.

drills.title: Channel defending
drills.setup: Mark a narrow channel eight metres wide and twenty long with a small goal at one end. The attacker starts at the open end with the ball, the defender starts on the goal line. The attacker tries to score, the defender to force them wide or win the ball. The narrow shape stops the defender from being beaten by pace alone and rewards good angles.
drills.coachingPoints: Close the space quickly while the ball travels; stay on your toes an arm's length away; tackle when the attacker's touch is heavy, not before.
drills.progression: Widen the channel to twelve metres so the defender must show one side deliberately.

drills.title: Recovery race
drills.setup: The attacker starts thirty metres from goal with the ball; the defender starts five metres behind them and only sets off on your whistle. The defender has to run the attacker down, get across their path, and either delay the shot or force them away from goal. Alternate which side the defender recovers from.
drills.coachingPoints: Run the shortest line to goal side, not at the ball; do not dive in from behind; once level, slow down and jockey.
drills.progression: Shorten the head start to two metres, or make it two attackers against one defender.

drills.title: Two against one delay
drills.setup: Two attackers start twenty-five metres from goal against one defender, with a five-second clock. The defender cannot win the game outright, so the job is to slow the attack, stay between the ball and goal, and hold off the tackle until the clock runs out. Rotate after each attempt so everybody defends twice.
drills.coachingPoints: Screen the pass while pressing the ball; retreat in a curve rather than straight back; talk to the keeper about who covers what.
drills.progression: Release a second defender after two seconds so the delay has a purpose.

drills.title: Pressing in pairs
drills.setup: A 20 by 20 metre square with three attackers passing on the outside and two defenders inside. The defenders must work as a pair: one presses the ball while the other cuts the nearest pass. Win the ball or force it out of the square and the defenders swap with the two nearest attackers. Ninety-second rounds.
drills.coachingPoints: Press the moment the ball travels; the second defender covers the shortest pass, not the ball; talk before you move.
drills.progression: Reduce the square to fifteen metres so pressing has to be even quicker.

drills.title: Defending the box
drills.setup: Mark a defensive zone in front of a small goal. Three defenders face four attackers who start from the halfway cone. The defenders' job is to keep a compact line, force the attack wide and clear the ball beyond the entry cone. Reset after every attempt and rotate the units after four attacks.
drills.coachingPoints: Stay within five metres of each other; nearest player presses, others tuck in; clear it wide and high, never across your own box.
drills.progression: Give the attackers a two-touch limit so defenders must react faster.

drills.title: Four goals, four against four
drills.setup: A pitch with two small cone goals on each end line, giving every team two targets to attack. Play four against four with the spare players rotating in every three minutes. Two goals per end pull defences apart and teach players to switch play towards the unguarded target.
drills.coachingPoints: Look up and pick the free goal; spread out when you win the ball; the nearest player presses, the rest cover.
drills.progression: A goal only counts if the ball has been in both halves of the pitch.

drills.title: Six against six, two touches
drills.setup: Use a pitch with a goal at one end and a small goal at the other, keeper in the big goal. Six against six with a two-touch limit for everybody. The touch limit forces players to look before the ball arrives and takes the game away from dribble-and-hope. Lift the restriction for the final three minutes.
drills.coachingPoints: First touch sets the pass; support at an angle, never behind the ball carrier; keep the pitch wide in possession.
drills.progression: One touch in your own half, unlimited in the final third.

drills.title: Three against three waves
drills.setup: A pitch with a small goal at each end and four teams of three waiting in a queue behind the touchline. Two teams play for ninety seconds or until a goal is scored, then the losing team leaves and the next wave comes straight on. Short, intense games with plenty of rest built in.
drills.coachingPoints: Play at full intensity, you get a rest soon; make a triangle whenever you have the ball; the waiting team gets ready on the line.
drills.progression: Winning team stays on for a maximum of three games in a row.

drills.title: Possession with a joker
drills.setup: An area with no goals. Two teams of six plus one joker who always plays for whoever has the ball, so possession is always seven against six. Ten consecutive passes scores a point. The overload guarantees a spare player somewhere, and the coaching is all about finding them.
drills.coachingPoints: Find the joker to break pressure; move after you pass; the team out of possession presses in pairs.
drills.progression: Shrink the area by five metres each way, or cap everyone at three touches.

drills.title: End-to-end transitions
drills.setup: A pitch with a small goal at each end, five against five with a ball supply beside each goal. As soon as a goal is scored or the ball leaves the pitch, you serve a new ball immediately to the team that did not have it. There are no stoppages, so players learn to reorganise while the game is still moving.
drills.coachingPoints: React to the turnover before you rest; nearest player to the ball presses; spread wide the moment you win it.
drills.progression: Serve the new ball into the space behind the defence.

drills.title: Two against two tournament
drills.setup: Three pitches of fifteen by twelve metres, each with two small goals, and six pairs playing two-minute games. Winning pairs move up a pitch, losing pairs move down, so games stay competitive. Everyone gets constant touches and has to defend as well as attack with nowhere to hide.
drills.coachingPoints: One presses, one covers; every attack starts with a pass or a dribble past your marker; keep the ball moving.
drills.progression: Play with one goal each so both pairs must attack a single target.

drills.title: Quick-feet cone ladder
drills.setup: Lay two lines of six cones one metre apart. Players work through them with a set pattern: two feet in each gap, then side steps, then in-and-out. Twenty seconds of work, forty seconds of rest, six rounds. Keep two lines running so nobody waits long and everyone gets full recovery between efforts.
drills.coachingPoints: On the toes, arms driving, chest up; quality of footwork before speed.
drills.progression: Finish each pattern with a five-metre sprint to a far cone.

drills.title: Shuttle turns with a ball
drills.setup: Cones at five, ten and fifteen metres from a start line. Players dribble out to the first cone, turn and come back, then repeat to the second and third. One full set is one repetition; work in pairs so one dribbles while the other recovers. Four repetitions each.
drills.coachingPoints: Decelerate before the turn; use the sole or outside of the foot to change direction; first touch out of the turn is a long one.
drills.progression: Turn out and finish with a pass into a teammate at the start line.

drills.title: Reaction colours
drills.setup: Four cones of different colours ten metres out from a central start point, with players in groups of three. Call a colour and the group sprints to that cone and back. Vary the gaps between calls so nobody can anticipate, and occasionally call two colours in sequence. Ten calls per group.
drills.coachingPoints: React on the word, not the movement of others; low first three steps; touch the cone and turn tight.
drills.progression: Number the cones instead and give simple sums, so the answer is the cone.

drills.title: Relay dribble circuit
drills.setup: Set a rectangular circuit of about sixty metres with a cone at each corner and a different task on each side: dribble, sprint with the ball, side-on dribble, sprint without the ball. Split into three relay teams; each player completes one lap and hands the ball to the next. Best of three laps per team.
drills.coachingPoints: Control before speed at the handover; run the corners tight; keep the ball within a stride at all times.
drills.progression: Add a slalom on one side, or make the handover a pass into the next runner's feet.

drills.title: Pyramid runs
drills.setup: Cones at ten, twenty, thirty and forty metres from a start line. Players run out to the first cone and back, then the second, and so on to the top of the pyramid before working back down. One pyramid is one set; work in three groups so two rest while one runs.
drills.coachingPoints: Turn tight at every cone; run through the line, do not slow before it; recovery walk, not standing still.
drills.progression: Carry a ball on the way out and leave it at the cone.

drills.title: Tag in the square
drills.setup: A square with three players wearing bibs as taggers. Everybody else moves freely inside; anyone tagged does five star jumps and rejoins. Ninety seconds per round, four rounds, changing taggers each time. The conditioning happens without anybody noticing they are running.
drills.coachingPoints: Change direction rather than sprint in straight lines; use the whole square; taggers work together to trap players in corners.
drills.progression: Tagged players freeze with arms out and can be freed by a teammate running under them.

drills.title: Set and save
drills.setup: Two servers ten metres out on either side of the goal, alternating firm shots along the ground into the corners. The keeper takes a small set step as each shot is struck, saves, returns the ball and resets to the middle. Ten saves, then a short break. Keep the shots hittable, not violent.
drills.coachingPoints: Feet set before the ball is struck; hands lead to the ball; use the body behind the hands where possible.
drills.progression: Servers disguise the side, or shoot at waist height for a different handling shape.

drills.title: Handling ladder
drills.setup: Keeper and partner face each other eight metres apart between two cones, no goal needed. Work through a ladder of services: rolled along the ground, waist height, chest height, above the head, then one bouncing awkwardly in front. Ten catches at each height before moving up. The keeper returns every ball with a throw the partner can catch.
drills.coachingPoints: W-shape hands above the waist, scoop below it; eyes on the ball all the way in; pull the ball into the chest once caught.
drills.progression: Partner calls the height only as the ball is released.

drills.title: Distribution under pressure
drills.setup: Two target players stand wide of the penalty area, with one presser starting twelve metres from the keeper. You play the ball to the keeper; the presser closes as soon as the ball is touched, and the keeper must control it and find whichever target is free. Six repetitions, alternating which side the pressure comes from.
drills.coachingPoints: Look before the ball arrives; first touch away from the presser; if both targets are covered, clear long and high.
drills.progression: Add a second presser so the keeper has one clear option at most.

drills.title: Crosses and claims
drills.setup: A server crosses from the corner of the penalty area while one attacker occupies the six-yard box. The keeper decides to come and claim, punch, or stay and hold the line, then calls the decision out loud. Start with unopposed crosses and only add the attacker once the keeper is catching cleanly. Eight crosses from each side.
drills.coachingPoints: Start off the goal line so you can move forward; call keeper or away loudly and early; catch at the highest point with one knee up for protection.
drills.progression: Two attackers and one defender, so the keeper reads a crowded box.

drills.title: Footwork and recover
drills.setup: Two cones four metres apart on the goal line. The keeper side-steps between them, touching each cone, then reacts to a low shot served from twelve metres as soon as they touch the second cone. Six repetitions, then rest. The movement before the save is the point, so keep the service honest and hittable.
drills.coachingPoints: Side-step, never cross the feet; get the feet set before the shot; recover to the middle of the goal every time.
drills.progression: Serve the shot to the side the keeper has just moved away from.

drills.title: One against one and breakaways
drills.setup: An attacker starts thirty metres out and runs at goal with the ball while the keeper decides when to come out, when to hold, and when to spread and block. Six repetitions with a short rest between each. Emphasise that a good decision made early beats a spectacular dive made late.
drills.coachingPoints: Come out while the ball is travelling away from the attacker's feet; stay big and low, hands down; do not commit until the attacker's head drops.
drills.progression: Add a second attacker in support so the keeper must also read the pass.
